A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARE framework and VWA-Adv study. The complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original agent attack and defense experiments in Section 5, plus CLIP ablations and synthetic screenshot experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental outcomes in Figures 4–7, Table 3, Figure 13, and Table 7, including the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3–5 retain the same ARE framework, attack objectives and procedures, agent configurations, and defenses. The inference-time-compute wording introduces no algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both use the same 200 VWA-Adv tasks across classifieds, shopping, and Reddit, the same text/image attack scenarios, and the same synthetic screenshot-selection task in Appendix C.2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Figures 4–7, including the four backbone LMs, agent configurations, and safety-prompt, abstention, paraphrase, and consistency defenses.

E3.justification: Task selection and starting states, success metrics, perturbation constraints, and evaluation settings are unchanged. Both specify two reflexion attempts and tree search with branching factor 3 and depth 1.

E4.justification: The component-isolation and defense analyses remain unchanged, as do the resolution, negative-text, and CLIP-ensemble ablations and screenshot-context analysis in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported results are retained. For example, Figure 6 still reports 31% ASR for the base configuration, 26% with an unattacked value function, and 38% when both components are attacked; Table 7 retains 71% for the full CLIP attack and 46% without negative text.

T1.justification: The agent-graph, adversarial-influence, and edge-weight definitions in Section 3 and the attack objectives in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract recasts the claim that adding components can harm robustness as a claim about inference-time compute. This modestly changes the headline framing while retaining the benchmark, ARE contribution, and up-to-67% attack-success claim.

C2.justification: The new joint summary after Section 5.3 explicitly interprets reflexion and tree search as examples of inference-time scaling decreasing worst-case robustness. v2 used separate component-specific summaries. The mechanism explanations and Appendix D limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical model identifiers, decoding settings, hardware, attack-text examples, and safety prompts. Code and data access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2 discussion, novelty statements, and explicit comparisons with prior agent-attack research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized abstract edits, combines two summaries, adds Cisco funding acknowledgment, and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header. The section structure and remaining prose are preserved.

P2.justification: Two shaded summary boxes on page 9 become one, moving the unchanged Figure 6 and Section 5.3 upward. The abstract and first reference page undergo local reflow; figure and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised abstract and combined summary emphasize inference-time compute, but the underlying component-level conclusions were already present in v2. Methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations are unchanged. The localized presentation and acknowledgment edits do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
